- When sentiment is consistently negative or bearish in recent history, model forecasts tend to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to account for subsequent volatility; cap upward momentum or add volatility buffer.
- In high-event periods (especially with net negative supply), model underestimates downside risk; increase downward drift or add bearish sentiment multiplier.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out false trends.
- In low-event or neutral sentiment periods, model often overestimates mean reversion; adjust for lagged momentum or add short-term volatility filter.
- When supply net is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish, model may overreact to bullish sentiment; dampen forecast growth by 10–20% relative to sentiment strength.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early event-driven volatility; add event-weighted volatility adjustment to first 7–10 days of forecast.
